questionText: When do you return 200 OK vs 201 Created vs 204 No Content?

target.learningOutcome: The learner can choose 200, 201, 204, or the nearby 202 response from the actual outcome and response content instead of memorizing a code per HTTP method.
inScope: Resource identification and the Location header on 201
Different successful outcomes for one PUT request
prerequisites: Basic HTTP headers and response content

claims.statement: A 200 OK response means the request succeeded, and except for CONNECT its content describes the result according to the request method; a 200 response is normally expected to contain content unless its framing says the length is zero.
A 201 Created response means the request was fulfilled and created one or more resources; Location identifies the primary created resource when present, otherwise the target URI identifies it.
A 204 No Content response means the request succeeded and there is no response content; response headers can still carry metadata about the result.
A successful PUT can return 201 when it creates the target, or 200 or 204 when it modifies an existing target, depending on whether response content is sent.
A 202 Accepted response says the request was accepted for processing but processing has not completed and might not eventually be performed.

Location identifies a resource in relation to the response, while Content-Location identifies the resource corresponding to the enclosed representation; their meanings are distinct even when their URI values match.

examples.title: 201 creation response followed by a separate 204 update response

validation.command: Parse each response independently and assert that the 201 body is valid JSON and that the 204 response ends after its headers
validation.expected: 201 includes Location and a JSON representation; 204 contains an ETag header and no response content

visuals.title: Completed success compared by creation and response content

notes: The lesson intentionally rejects one-status-per-method shortcuts by carrying one PUT target through three successful outcomes.
The 201 example uses Location because it helps the learner, while the prose correctly states that Location is not mandatory in every 201 response.

review.notes: Success status, Location, no-content, PUT, and 202 boundary claims were checked against RFC 9110; both responses parsed and the table matches their outcome boundaries.
